pageCache.pageTitle: Careers and Post 16 | Trinity Secondary Lewisham
pageCache.text:
Careers and Post 16
Preparing for life beyond Trinity
Helping pupils explore possibilities, understand their strengths and make confident choices about what comes next.
From choosing subjects to considering sixth form, college, apprenticeships or future careers, pupils make increasingly important decisions as they move through Secondary school. At Trinity, careers education helps pupils understand their interests, strengths and ambitions, explore different possibilities and connect what they are learning now with where it could take them in the future. Because Trinity does not have a Sixth Form, impartial guidance is particularly important. Pupils are supported to consider a broad range of Post 16 routes and make informed choices about their next step.
Thinking ahead: pupils are encouraged to explore possibilities early, ask questions and take an active role in planning their future.
Careers guidance at Trinity
Careers education develops as pupils move through Secondary school. Trinity has an onsite independent careers adviser who supports pupils through careers information, group sessions and individual guidance. Pupils receive group careers sessions in Year 8 and one to one careers sessions in Year 10.
Key Stage 3, exploring possibilities
During Key Stage 3, pupils begin exploring careers, skills and different pathways. They are encouraged to think about what interests them, recognise their strengths and understand that there are many different routes into further study, training and employment.
Key Stage 4, making informed choices
During Key Stage 4, careers guidance becomes increasingly focused on the decisions pupils will make beyond Year 11. Pupils consider Post 16 pathways, entry requirements, applications, work experience and how their current choices connect with their longer term ambitions.
Understanding strengths and ambitions
Good careers guidance is personal. There is no single pathway that is right for every pupil. Pupils are encouraged to consider what they enjoy, what they are good at, what motivates them and the kind of future they might want to build.
Questions pupils are encouraged to explore
What do I enjoy?
What am I good at?
What motivates me?
Which subjects interest me?
What qualifications or training might I need?
What opportunities are available locally and nationally?
Year 10 work experience
Work experience gives pupils an opportunity to experience the world of work first hand. In Year 10, pupils are encouraged and supported to find their own placement. Taking responsibility for this process helps pupils think carefully about their interests and begin making connections with employers and workplaces. During their placement, pupils can develop practical skills including communication, organisation, teamwork, problem solving, confidence and independence. The experience also gives them an opportunity to reflect on what they enjoy and what they might want from their future working life.
Experience the workplace: Year 10 work experience helps pupils connect school with the world beyond it and develop skills in a real working environment.
Preparing for Post 16
As pupils approach the end of Year 11, we help them understand the different routes available and make choices that reflect their strengths, interests and future goals. Post 16 pathways may include:
Pupils are supported to understand the differences between these pathways and consider which options may suit them best.
sixth forms
colleges
apprenticeships
A levels
T Levels
vocational courses
other training routes
Meeting colleges and providers
Hearing directly from Post 16 providers helps pupils understand the choices available beyond Trinity. We invite a range of providers into school so that pupils can learn about different courses and pathways, compare opportunities and ask questions. Families are also encouraged to attend open events at sixth forms, colleges and training providers. Visiting different settings can help pupils understand what each option offers before deciding where to apply.
From exploring to applying
Choosing a Post 16 destination involves more than deciding on a course. Pupils are supported to think carefully about the practical steps involved in moving on from Trinity.
Applications and next steps
Support may include:
Families can support pupils by discussing options early, attending open events and helping them keep track of important deadlines.
researching different pathways and providers
attending open events
understanding entry requirements
preparing applications
writing personal statements where required
preparing for interviews
considering travel, course structure and support
making final decisions after offers are received
Explore careers and the world of work
Pupils and families can use trusted careers resources to research jobs, sectors, qualifications, skills and future opportunities.
Explore Careers

We welcome opportunities for pupils to learn from employers, colleges, training providers, apprenticeship providers and members of the wider community. If you are an employer or provider who would like to contribute to careers education at Trinity, please contact the school office.

pageCache.text:
Culture, Behaviour and Pastoral Care
Known, supported and ready to learn
High expectations, strong relationships and pastoral care work together to help pupils feel secure, confident and ready to succeed.
Parents want to know that their child will be noticed, cared for and guided through the challenges and opportunities of Secondary school. At Trinity, pupils are part of a community where adults know them, expectations are clear and support is available when they need it. We want pupils to work hard, behave well and aim high, while growing in confidence, character, responsibility and ambition.
High expectations with care: pupils are supported to work hard, treat others with respect, take responsibility and grow into confident members of the Trinity community.
A calm and purposeful school
Clear routines, consistent expectations and positive relationships help create an environment where pupils can concentrate on learning. Pupils are supported to understand what good behaviour looks like, why it matters and how their choices affect other people. Our expectations are built around respect, responsibility and care for the wider community.
High expectations with care
At Trinity, behaviour is not simply about following rules. It is also part of learning to take responsibility and developing character. We recognise that young people sometimes make mistakes and need guidance. Staff help pupils reflect on their choices, understand their impact and move forward positively. Where appropriate, pupils are supported to repair harm and rebuild relationships.
How pupils are known and supported
Smaller communities and trusted relationships help pupils find their place within Trinity Secondary.
Family Groups and daily belonging
Family Groups give pupils a smaller daily community within the wider Secondary school. Family Group leaders see pupils regularly and provide a consistent point of contact. This time helps pupils settle, prepare for learning, raise concerns and develop positive habits. Family Group time also supports reading, PSHE, character development, revision skills, community awareness and wider personal development.
Houses and smaller communities
Every pupil belongs to a House, creating another smaller community within the wider Trinity family.
Our five houses at the secondary are:
Through Houses, pupils can take part in competitions, challenges, charity work, leadership opportunities and events that celebrate effort, teamwork and contribution.
Recognising positive choices
Praise, encouragement and rewards help pupils understand that effort, kindness, resilience and contribution matter. Positive behaviour is recognised through classroom praise, House points, leadership opportunities, participation in events and celebrating pupils who demonstrate Trinity values in action.
Support when it is needed
Growing through Secondary school is not always straightforward. Pupils may sometimes need additional help with learning, friendships, wellbeing or circumstances beyond the classroom. Pastoral care at Trinity begins with knowing pupils well. When support is needed, staff work together with pupils and families to understand the concern and consider the appropriate next steps.
Pastoral and wellbeing support & Useful Contacts
Support may involve Family Group leaders, Heads of Year, senior staff, mentoring, wellbeing support, SEND support or communication with parents and carers. Where appropriate, additional support may include counselling, mindfulness, emotional regulation strategies, targeted interventions or support from external agencies. Pupils are encouraged to speak to a trusted adult when something is worrying them.

Safeguarding and SEND
Safeguarding is central to school life at Trinity. We are committed to promoting pupils’ welfare and providing an environment where concerns can be shared and responded to appropriately. Some pupils may also need additional support with learning, communication, emotional regulation or sensory needs. Further information is available through our Safeguarding and SEND pages.
Pupils have a voice
Pupils are active members of the Trinity community, not simply recipients of it. Through Trinity Voice, buddies, peer mentors, Wellbeing Ambassadors and other leadership opportunities, pupils can support others, share ideas and contribute to school life. These opportunities help pupils develop confidence, empathy, responsibility and leadership while strengthening the sense that everyone has a part to play.
Working with families
Strong pastoral care works best when school and home work together. Parents and carers know their children well, and we value communication with families when questions or concerns arise. Where a pupil needs additional help, school and home can work together to understand the concern and consider the appropriate support.
A culture where pupils can flourish
Culture, behaviour and pastoral care are not separate from learning. They help make successful learning possible. From Year 7 to Year 11, pupils are encouraged to work hard, treat others well, take responsibility, seek help when they need it and contribute positively to their community. Our aim is for pupils to leave Trinity as confident, capable and compassionate young people, ready for their next step.

pageCache.text:
Learning and Curriculum
Learning that builds towards the future
An ambitious Secondary curriculum that helps pupils build knowledge, confidence and independence from Year 7 to Year 11.
At Trinity Secondary, pupils study a broad curriculum designed to build knowledge, skills and understanding over time. From the foundations established in Year 7 to the increasing independence and specialisation of Key Stage 4, pupils are encouraged to think deeply, communicate confidently and develop the knowledge and habits they need for GCSEs and what comes next.
Learning that builds over time: pupils develop subject knowledge, vocabulary, confidence and independence as they move through Secondary school.
The Secondary learning journey
Years 7 and 8
Year 9
Years 10 and 11
How to use this page
The curriculum information below shows what pupils study by year group and subject. On mobile, simply select a year group and then open the subject you would like to explore. Some subjects in Years 9, 10 and 11 form part of option or pathway provision, so not every pupil will study every subject listed.
For more information about a particular subject, please contact the school office and your enquiry will be directed to the relevant curriculum leader.
Key Stage 4 courses
At Key Stage 4, pupils study a core curriculum alongside GCSE and pathway subjects.
Courses and subjects
English, Mathematics, Science, Religious Education and Core Physical Education
Humanities and languages
Geography, History, French and Spanish
Creative, practical and technical subjects
Art, Drama, Engineering, Food Preparation and Nutrition, Computer Science, iMedia, Photography, Music and Music Technology
Physical education and sport pathways
GCSE Physical Education and Sport Studies
Additional pathway subjects
Business Studies, Statistics and Citizenship
Curriculum by year group
Year 7, building strong foundations
Year 7 helps pupils make a confident start to Secondary learning. Pupils study a broad curriculum while becoming familiar with specialist teaching, subject vocabulary, independent learning and the habits needed for future study.
Year 8, deepening knowledge and confidence
Year 8 builds on the knowledge and skills developed in Year 7. Learning becomes increasingly demanding as pupils strengthen subject vocabulary, analysis, problem solving and their confidence in applying what they know.
Year 9, growing independence and GCSE readiness
Year 9 helps pupils grow in independence and readiness for Key Stage 4. Pupils work with increasingly complex ideas and develop the knowledge, vocabulary and study habits that prepare them for GCSE courses.
Year 10, beginning Key Stage 4
Year 10 marks the beginning of Key Stage 4. Pupils continue their core curriculum alongside more specialised GCSE and pathway learning, developing deeper knowledge and increasingly independent study habits.
Year 11, GCSEs and next steps
Year 11 brings together the knowledge and skills pupils have developed throughout Secondary. Pupils complete their courses, consolidate learning, prepare for examinations and make informed decisions about what comes next.
Beyond the curriculum
Learning at Trinity extends beyond individual subjects. Wider opportunities give pupils different ways to develop their interests, confidence, character and leadership while putting what they learn into practice.
Beyond Lessons
Looking Ahead
Find out more about the curriculum
If you would like more information about the curriculum in a particular subject or year group, please contact the school office. Your enquiry will be directed to the relevant curriculum leader. pageCache.pageTitle: Exams and Revision | Trinity Secondary Lewisham
pageCache.text:
Exams and Revision
Preparing with confidence
Exam information, practical guidance and revision strategies to help pupils prepare effectively.
Assessments and examinations are an important part of Secondary school, but successful preparation is not about last minute cramming. At Trinity, pupils are encouraged to build good habits over time, revisit important knowledge regularly, practise applying what they know and ask for help when they need it.
Prepare steadily, not suddenly: regular revision, effective routines and asking for support early can help pupils approach assessments with greater confidence.
PPEs and assessments
PPEs, or pre public examinations, help pupils practise the routines and expectations of formal examinations. They give pupils opportunities to experience exam conditions, practise managing their time, identify what they know securely and recognise where further revision may be needed. PPEs also help teachers understand where pupils may need further teaching, practice or support.
Year 11
Year 11 Revision Resources
Preparing effectively
Good revision begins with a realistic plan. Pupils should start early enough to revisit topics several times rather than trying to cover everything immediately before an assessment.
Build a revision routine
A revision timetable can help pupils decide what to study and when. A useful plan should be realistic, identify particular subjects or topics and include time for breaks, exercise, meals and rest. Shorter regular sessions can be more manageable than trying to complete several hours of revision at once.
Retrieval practice and flashcards
Effective revision involves trying to bring knowledge back from memory rather than simply reading notes repeatedly. Pupils can answer questions, complete quizzes, explain a topic aloud, cover their notes and write down what they remember, or ask somebody to test them. Flashcards can also support retrieval. Questions can be written on one side and answers on the other. Cards pupils find difficult should be revisited more frequently, while secure knowledge can be reviewed less often.
Spaced practice and interleaving
Spaced practice means spreading revision over time and returning regularly to previous learning. Interleaving means revisiting different topics or types of questions rather than spending a very long period working on only one area. A well planned revision timetable can help pupils use both approaches.
Visuals, examples and deeper thinking
Different approaches can help pupils organise and understand knowledge. Diagrams, timelines, symbols, mind maps and labelled drawings can be used alongside written information to help pupils make connections. Worked examples, model answers and past paper questions can help pupils see how knowledge is applied. Pupils can also strengthen understanding by asking questions such as: Why does this happen? How does this connect with something I already know? How would I explain this to somebody else?
Focused revision sessions
Some pupils find it useful to divide revision into short periods of focused work followed by brief breaks. One approach is the Pomodoro method: 25 minutes of focused revision followed by a 5 minute break, repeated several times before taking a longer break. The important principle is to use revision time purposefully while allowing regular opportunities to rest and reset.
Families can help
Parents and carers do not need to become subject experts to support effective revision. Families can help pupils establish realistic routines, identify somewhere suitable to study where possible, encourage regular breaks and ask pupils to explain what they have been learning. Encouraging pupils to start early and seek help when they are unsure can be particularly valuable.
Wellbeing during exams
Examination periods can feel demanding. Preparing carefully should sit alongside looking after physical and emotional wellbeing. Pupils should aim to get enough sleep, eat properly, stay active, take appropriate breaks and avoid trying to revise throughout the night. If a pupil is worried or feels overwhelmed, they should speak to a trusted adult rather than trying to manage the concern alone.
Support in school
Teachers will guide pupils on what to revise, which resources to use and how to prepare for assessments in their subjects. Pupils should speak to their subject teacher if they are unsure about content or revision. They can also speak to their Family Group Leader, Head of Year or another trusted adult if they need wider support.
Looking beyond Year 11
Examinations are an important milestone, but they are also part of a wider journey. Alongside preparing for GCSEs, pupils are supported to consider their Post 16 choices and the pathways available beyond Trinity.
Contact us
For questions about examinations, assessments or revision, please contact the school office and your enquiry will be directed to the appropriate member of staff. Secondary Phase: Trinity Secondary, Taunton Road, Lee, London, SE12 8PD Telephone: 020 8852 3191 Email: admin@trinity.lewisham.sch.uk
